name: advection_plume_phase
title: Advection plume-reach phase diagram
claim: The downstream reach of the growing biomass plume scales monotonically with advection strength — an advection-controlled spatial-transport phase relationship.

purpose.question: How far downstream does the biomass plume reach as a function of the advection strength of the COMETS field?
purpose.mechanism: Parameter-sweep phase-diagram study (discovery engine): a real composite swept over one axis, reduced to a regime metric.
purpose.expected_outcome: The metric varies monotonically across the swept axis, revealing the regime relationship.

question: How far downstream does the biomass plume reach as a function of the advection strength of the COMETS field?

behavior_tests.name: ADVECTION-PLUME-REACH-INCREASES
behavior_tests.description: the biomass plume's downstream centroid reach increases monotonically with advection strength.

ADVECTION-PLUME-REACH-INCREASES.detail: increasing; steps [1.409,2.614]; net +5.758; start 0.05638 end 5.815; tol 0.01

findings.statement: The plume's downstream centroid advances from ~0 (no advection) to ~5.8 rows at the strongest advection: transport strength, not metabolism, sets how far the growing population spreads across the field.

resolved: Plume downstream reach scales monotonically with advection strength.
remaining: Whether diffusion blurs or sharpens the plume boundary at fixed advection is unquantified.

followup_study_proposals.motivation: At fixed advection, sweeping diffusion would show whether the plume front stays sharp or disperses — a 2D transport phase diagram.

falsifiability: If plume reach were flat or non-monotonic in advection strength, the advection-controlled-transport claim would be false.
limitations: Advection varied along one axis at fixed diffusion; a single composite and horizon.

alternative_hypotheses.hypothesis: The plume reach reflects diffusion, not advection.
alternative_hypotheses.excluded_by: Diffusion is held fixed across the sweep; only the advection vector varies.
